business_scope.primary_industry_name: Bonded Warehouse Operations in Customs Free Trade Zones

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (Confederation level; incorporation and registration within the Canton of Zug, Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic; Swiss Civil Code SR 210 and Code of Obligations SR 220; federal-Cantonal commercial register system; notarial mandatory incorporation)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Swiss Confederation and the People's Republic of China on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (signed 16.11.1986; in force 13.03.1987)
Convention between Switzerland and China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation on Income and Capital (signed 06.07.1990; in force 13.09.1991; as amended by the 2013 Protocol)
Free Trade Agreement between the EFTA States and China (in force 01.07.2014; Switzerland is an EFTA member)
Switzerland maintains a global network of approximately 120 BITs and 90+ DTAAs; umbrella protections under the ICSID and Swiss Investment Promotion Agreements apply as applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA/GwG), SR 955.0, Articles 4 (beneficial owner identification), 6 (politically exposed persons) and 9 (reporting duty to MROS); Swiss Criminal Code (StGB/CP), SR 311.0, Articles 305bis and 305ter (money laundering and negligence in financial transactions); Code of Obligations (OR/CO), SR 220, Articles 697j-697l (mandatory company-level register of beneficial owners at 25% threshold), 950-951 (firm name law), 621, 626, 629 and 632 (minimum capital and incorporation); Federal Act on the Enforcement of International Sanctions (Embargo Act), SR 946.231; Financial Market Supervision Act (FINMAG), SR 956.1; Federal Council Dispatch 23.060 of 30 August 2023 on the partial AMLA revision proposing a central federal UBO register remains pending, so the operative mechanism is the internal company UBO register under CO Article 697j.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport or national identity document of each beneficial owner, director and signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport/identity authority of the individual's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for apostille member states, e.g., PRC documents apostilled by the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs) OR Consular Legalization (for non-member states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial owner self-declaration and source-of-wealth declaration (Selbstdeklaration der wirtschaftlich Berechtigten)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Signing UBO before a Swiss notary public or licensed fiduciary; foreign signatures must be notarized and apostilled/consularized in the country of signature
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (depending on signatory jurisdiction)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Company Register Extract of each corporate shareholder or ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction (e.g., PRC State Administration for Market Regulation or its online enterprise registry)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (Generalvollmacht) granted to the Swiss incorporation agent and Swiss counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Principal and all beneficial owners, certified through notarial act in the country of execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source-of-funds evidence, bank reference letter and corporate structure chart including all intermediate layers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or financial intermediary of the transferor; corporate chart certified by the parent company secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization; internal CDD acceptance by the Swiss fiduciary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory CDD under AMLA: positive identification of all UBOs, authorized signatories and intermediate entities; PEP screening under AMLA Article 6 including family members and close associates; mandatory screening against the Swiss SECO consolidated sanctions register, the UN Security Council sanctions lists, the EU consolidated sanctions list and, where USD clearing or US counterparties are involved, the US OFAC SDN list; negative media and adverse information check; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation for every UBO; any suspicion is reportable to the Money Laundering Reporting Office Switzerland (MROS) within 10 working days under AMLA Article 9; risk-rating refresh at least annually for the Medium-Risk Enhanced tier; CDD records retained for 10 years per AMLA Article 14.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix (Zentraler Firmenindex) of the Federal Department of Justice and Police; official preliminary name clearance is obtained through the Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug) which issues a Vorbescheinigung (name reservation certificate); the German-language SHAB (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt) publishes the subsequent incorporation notice.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The firm name must be written in Latin script and composed of a freely chosen element plus a mandatory legal-form suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft', 'AG', 'Société Anonyme', 'SA', 'Società Anonima' or 'SA' (CO Article 950). Non-Latin script names (e.g., Chinese) must be transliterated phonetically into one of the official Swiss languages (German, French, Italian or Romansh); the original script may appear only as a graphical supplement, never as the registered firm. The name must not be misleading or contrary to public interest (CO Article 944 para. 2bis) and must be clearly distinguishable from all prior registered firms (CO Article 951).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banker, Privatbank, Sparkasse (FINMA banking licence required)
Versicherung, Assurance, Rückversicherung (FINMA insurance licence required)
Fonds, Invest, Anlagestiftung (collective investment licence required)
Trust, Treuhand, Fiduciaire (licensed fiduciary/trust supervision scrutiny)
Eidgenossenschaft, Bund, Confédération, Confœderatio (sovereign state symbols)
Swiss, Schweizer, Suisse, Svizzera (national brand protection; requires demonstrated genuine connection to Switzerland)
Zolllager, Freihafen (customs warehousing terms; requires FOCBS licence or explicit customs authority clearance)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the cantonal commercial register office rejects the name, the applicant may: (a) request a formal written ruling (Verfügung) stating the grounds of refusal; (b) file an administrative objection with the cantonal supervisory authority for the commercial register of Zug within 30 days of service of the ruling; (c) appeal further to the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht, St. Gallen) within 30 days; and (d) in parallel, file an amended name proposal with the registry. The Vorbescheinigung may be renewed once for an additional 60 days by written application before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A purely virtual office is not permissible as the sole registered seat of a Swiss AG because the statutory seat must be the place of effective administration (CO Article 626). Commercial domiciliation services in Zug may provide a correspondence address only if central administration and decision-making are demonstrably located in Switzerland. For the bonded warehouse licence, the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS/BAZG) mandates physical, secure and access-controlled warehouse premises within a customs free zone or bonded depot; a virtual office will cause licence refusal and trigger substance scrutiny by the tax administration and the commercial register.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 90% plus – FOCBS performs scheduled and unannounced physical inspections of licensed bonded depots at least annually, including stock verification, sealing checks and record inspection; the cantonal tax authority and the commercial register may also conduct on-site substance verifications during the first 12 months of operation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal fee schedule for the commercial register; standard fee CHF 60-120

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Public notarization of the articles of association (Statuten), incorporation minutes and share issuance declarations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff scaled by share capital; CHF 500-900 prevailing benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial register entry fee for the Aktiengesellschaft
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal tariff under the Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV); CHF 300-700

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of incorporation in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB/FOSC)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official gazette publication tariff; CHF 180-260 per incorporation notice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization fees for four foreign corporate/UBO document bundles (e.g., PRC parent documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the issuing state (e.g., PRC MFA apostille post-7 November 2023) and Swiss cantonal apostille authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Apostille Convention fixed national fees plus notarial and courier costs; USD 20-50 per apostille

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO piercing, PEP/OFAC/UN/SECO sanctions screening, CDD file construction and KYC review by licensed Swiss fiduciary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Swiss fiduciary (Treuhandgesellschaft) / corporate services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed fee CHF 1,500-3,000 for Medium-Risk Enhanced CDD

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss bank / licensed securities dealer holding the SIX blocked account
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: CO Article 632 para. 1; CHF 50,000 blocked and released only upon notary confirmation of incorporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Customs bonded warehouse licence application and customs guarantee set-up at FOCBS
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS/BAZG), Customs Surveillance Directorate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Customs administration fee schedule; CHF 800-1,500 licence processing plus potential security bond

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and commercial substance arrangement for first year (domiciliation in Zug plus physical bonded depot premises)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed domiciliation provider in Zug and free trade zone operator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark CHF 2,500-4,000 per year for combined registered seat and operational address

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Swiss legal counsel fees for incorporation, name clearance defence, UBO declaration review and licence pre-consultation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hourly rate CHF 300-500; fixed incorporation package CHF 4,000-8,000 prevailing market benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR; SR 220), Articles 620-763 on the Aktiengesellschaft (stock corporation), in particular Arts. 626, 629 and 632 (articles of association, notarization and paid-up capital); Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV; SR 221.411); Federal Act on the Amendment of the Swiss Civil Code (Part Five: Company Registry Provisions).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of the Registered Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce), operating through the egreg electronic filing platform and the Swiss Central Business Name Index (Zefix).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Deed of Incorporation (Errichtungsprotokoll) with Articles of Association (Statuten), accompanied by the Declaration for Commercial Register Entry (Eingabebogen) submitted to the Cantonal Commercial Register Office.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum authorized share capital of CHF 100,000; at least CHF 50,000 must be paid up in cash at incorporation and deposited in a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) at a licensed Swiss bank, evidenced by an unqualified bank capital confirmation (Liberierungsbestätigung) attached to the registration filing. Alternatively, the articles may provide for CHF 50,000 authorized capital fully paid in. Released only after Commercial Register entry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [FULL COMPANY NAME] AG, adopted in writing on [DATE] pursuant to Articles 698 and 716a of the Swiss Code of Obligations.

WHEREAS the founders subscribed 1,000 registered shares of CHF 100.00 nominal value each and deposited CHF 100,000.00 into the blocked capital account No. [reference] at [Swiss bank], bank confirmation attached;

NOW BE IT RESOLVED:
1. The subscription and allotment are ratified.
2. The registered office is fixed at [street], [postal code] [canton], Switzerland; the articles approved.
3. [Name] is appointed President and [Name] Secretary, each individually; auditors [firm] are appointed.
4. The President is authorized to execute Commercial Register filings and initiate VAT and Customs Warehouse licensing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Association and Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public or authorized attorney-at-law empowered to execute authentic deeds under cantonal notarial law in the canton of the registered office (e.g., Notariat des Kantons Zürich).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association covering company name (with AG or SA suffix), registered office address in the canton, corporate purpose strictly limited to bonded warehouse, customs logistics and complementary storage services, share capital of CHF 100,000 divided into 1,000 registered shares of CHF 100.00 nominal value, board organization, signature rules and auditors. Book a notarization appointment; present original passports and foreign police clearances or residence permits as applicable; the notary verifies identity and legal capacity, reads the deed aloud and executes the authentic instrument in the official language of the canton (German, French or Italian). Request sufficient notarial certified copies for Commercial Register, bank and customs filings.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association (Statuten)
Valid passport or national identity card of each founder
Notarial certification of signatures
Founder consent declarations for board appointments
Proof of address and, if applicable, foreign residence permits
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses authentication due to defective or contradictory articles, correct the deficiencies, re-draft the articles and re-submit for a new authentic deed; a formal refusal letter, if issued, may be challenged before the cantonal supervising notarial authority, but a complete re-filing is ordinarily expedient.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Account and Bank Capital Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-licensed Swiss bank maintaining corporate accounts, e.g., Zuercher Kantonalbank or equivalent commercial bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the bank for a blocked capital account (Sperrkonto) in the name of the future company designated as [Company] AG i.E. Submit the preliminary articles, deed copy, beneficial ownership declarations and AML/KYC documentation. Transfer at least CHF 50,000 (or the full CHF 100,000) from the founders' accounts by wire transfer with exact payment references. Instruct the bank to issue an irrevocable capital confirmation (Liberierungsbestätigung) stating the account holder, amount credited, blockage condition and release-authorization clause; the original signed confirmation must accompany the Commercial Register application.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of notarized incorporation deed and articles
KYC/beneficial ownership forms under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG)
Founder passport copies and source-of-funds evidence
Subscription list of registered shares
Wire transfer payment instructions referencing the blocked account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank applies enhanced due diligence or discounts a source-of-funds enquiry, provide corroborated bank statements, business resumes and source-of-wealth documentation within the bank's requested timeline; if confirmation is unreasonably withheld, close the account and re-open a Sperrkonto with an alternative FINMA-licensed bank, ensuring the substituted confirmation is issued before the registration deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register Entry Application and Federal UID Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons der Sitzgemeinde) via the egreg electronic filing portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the electronic application through egreg accompanied by: the notarized deed and articles; the bank capital confirmation; handwritten signature specimens of all directors and authorized signatories (certified); declarations of acceptance signed by board members; the auditor's consent declaration; and the UID declaration form notifying the Federal Statistical Office. The registrar performs the prima facie legality review; upon approval the company acquires the Swiss UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) and the entry is published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB), conferring legal personality.
required_dossiers: Notarized incorporation deed and Statuten
Bank capital confirmation (Liberierungsbestätigung)
Certified handwritten signature specimens of directors
Written acceptances of board and audit appointments
Auditor's consent declaration (if mandatory audit)
Completed UID registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a formal deficiency notice (Nachforderung) or preliminary objection, cure the particular defect within the statutory deadline (usually 30 days) and resubmit the corrected documents via egreg; an entry refusal may be appealed to the cantonal commercial court (Handelsgericht / Rekursbehörde) within 10 days of service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Tax and VAT (MWST) Registration with Employer Social Insurance Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (FTA / ESTV), VAT Main Division, Schwarztorstrasse 50, 3003 Bern; Cantonal Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse) for AHV/AVS.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following the Commercial Register entry, obtain the Zefix extract reflecting the new UID and submit the VAT liability registration to ESTV through the electronic AINV service using form 310; registration is mandatory where annual taxable turnover from warehousing, handling and logistics services reaches CHF 100,000, or electable for smaller companies. Simultaneously notify the competent cantonal compensation office for AHV/IV/EO employer registration and obtain the employer identification number for payroll deductions and accident insurance (SUVA) coverage.
required_dossiers: Zefix / Commercial Register extract with UID
ESTV VAT registration form 310 or AINV electronic declaration
Projected turnover statement for first business year
Board authorization for tax representatives
Shareholder register extract for UID confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ESTV challenges the turnover threshold or applies retroactive VAT liability, file a formal objection (Einsprache) within 30 days accompanied by signed warehouse contracts and export documentation; if the compensation office delays AHV enrollment, request an interim provisional employer number and escalate to the Federal Social Insurance Office (BSV) for administrative intercession.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fire Safety Clearance, Structural Load Inspection and Occupational Health Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Fire Insurance Authority (Kantonale Gebäudeversicherung / Brandversicherung), Cantonal Building Inspection Office (Baukontrolle) and SUVA (Schweizerische Unfallversicherungsanstalt).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the fire safety certificate for the bonded depot premises, verifying compliance with VKF model fire protection guidelines (sprinkler system, fire doors, hazardous-goods storage segregation). Secure the structural load approval confirming floor-loading capacity for racked goods. File the workplace notification and ArGV 3 occupational safety declaration with SUVA, attaching the warehouse layout, employee roster, safety concept and emergency plan; receive SUVA's confirmation of occupational health supervision before operations commence.
required_dossiers: Building permit and approved floor plans
Fire protection concept and VKF compliance report
Structural static load certificate for racking and storage zones
Employee register and SUVA insurance confirmation
ArGV 3 workplace checklist and emergency plan
Hazardous substances storage declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire inspector identifies deficiencies (e.g., missing fire compartmentation), execute the required remediation works and obtain a re-inspection certificate; if SUVA notes workplace non-compliance, implement the corrective action plan and request a follow-up audit, with the right of appeal to the cantonal administrative court for any unlawful condition attached to clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Customs Warehouse Authorization (Zolllager / Bonded Depot) Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS / BAZG – Bundesamt für Zoll und Grenzsicherheit), Customs Directorate, Monbijoustrasse 40, 3003 Bern.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the customs warehouse authorization application per Articles 54-58 of the Swiss Customs Act (Zollgesetz) and Article 55 Zollverordnung, specifying the bonded warehouse scope for storage of non-union goods under customs supervision with suspended duties and taxes. Attach the site plan, the electronic inventory control system description (NCTS-compatible), physical security concept (CCTV, perimeter fencing, access control), annual stocktaking procedure and the financial solvency evidence. The authorization is premise-specific and requires SHAB/UED and UID references; approvals are generally granted for multi-year renewable terms.
required_dossiers: Customs warehouse application form (Bewilligungsgesuch)
Commercial Register extract and UID certificate
Site plan, lease or title deed and layout drawings
Electronic inventory control system specification
Security concept with CCTV and access control details
Fire safety certificate and SUVA confirmation
Financial statements or bank solvency reference
Description of proposed burden and relief procedures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If FOCBS requests further particulars under the duty of cooperation, respond in writing within 30 days; if the application is formally refused, request a reviewable ruling (Verfügung) and appeal to the competent customs area directorate, ultimately to the Federal Administrative Court in St. Gallen within 30 days of notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS / BAZG – Bundesamt für Zoll und Grenzsicherheit), Swiss Customs Administration; supplementary supervision by the cantonal commercial and building inspectorates.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Customs Warehouse Authorization (Zolllagerbewilligung / autorisation d'entrepôt douanier) for a bonded depot under Articles 54-58 Zollgesetz (SR 631.0) and Article 55 Zollverordnung (SR 631.01).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / BAFU – Bundesamt für Umwelt), Worblentalstrasse 68, CH-3063 Ittigen; implementation delegated to the cantonal environmental protection office.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Compulsory Preliminary Assessment (Voruntersuchung) under Annex 1 No. 40.5 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV / OEIE) when the bonded storage facility's gross floor area reaches 20,000 m² or when hazardous goods are stored in substantial quantities; otherwise a simple environmental registration with the cantonal environmental authority suffices.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater from wash bays and sanitary facilities must meet Annex 3.2 of the Waters Protection Ordinance (GSchV): COD ≤ 60 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 20 mg/L, TSS ≤ 20 mg/L; VOC emissions from handling, decanting and tank ventilation must comply with the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV) aggregate limit of 20 mg/m³ total carbon; hazardous waste, used packaging and contaminated absorbents must be traceable and disposed of per the Waste Ordinance (VVEA) with a full audit trail for customs-excise goods.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the cantonal fire insurance authority under VKF model guidelines, comprising fire-resistant construction, sprinkler coverage and hazardous-goods segregation; structural load and static inspection by the cantonal building office confirming the floor capacity for high-density racked storage; SUVA occupational safety confirmation under the Accident Insurance Act (UVG) and Occupational Safety Ordinance (ArGV 3) covering workplace layout, mechanical handling equipment and employee training; civil defense (Zivilschutz) building obligations, including any required shelter areas and access routes, verified during the building permit procedure.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung – ESTV; Administration fédérale des contributions – AFC), official multi-lingual VAT portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch (VAT e-fiscal platform, 'Mehrwertsteuer/TVA' online filing). Complementary registries: Central Business Name Index (Zefix) and the Swiss Business Identifier (UID) registry at https://www.uid.admin.ch.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A newly formed Swiss AG is filed with the cantonal Commercial Register (Handelsregister), which generates the Swiss UID (format CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx) as the universal business identification. VAT registration must then be submitted electronically to the ESTV via the official VAT registration form (Form 15 'Registrierung zur Mehrwertsteuer / Inscription à la TVA'); the UID becomes the VAT number supplemented by the MWST/TVA/IVA suffix. A foreign entity with no Swiss seat must appoint a fiscal representative (Steuervertretung/représentant fiscal) domiciled in Switzerland and file the simplified non-resident registration form with the ESTV; the same UID-VAT number procedure applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland has no US-style check-the-box election; an Aktiengesellschaft is mandatorily subject to entity-level federal direct tax and cantonal/communal corporate tax, with shareholders taxed only on distributions. Available statutory mechanisms: (i) small-business exemption election under art. 25 VAT Act for turnover below CHF 100,000; (ii) optional VAT taxation (Option) on real estate and certain inter-affiliate supplies; (iii) notional interest deduction (NID) and patent-box elections on qualifying income; (iv) hybrid-financing instruments are decoupled per Swiss domestic anti-hybrid provisions, but no elective entity-status classification exists for treaty purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT / GST / Sales and Use Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of annual worldwide taxable turnover (excluding exempt supplies) per arts. 10–11 of the Swiss VAT Act; businesses below the threshold may register voluntarily unless they cross-border supply inbound services subject to the acquirer-reverse-charge mechanism. Non-resident suppliers of digital and electronically supplied services to Swiss private consumers (B2C) must register from the first franc (single registration threshold of CHF 100,000 is not applied to them).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not impose government-run real-time fiscal clearance, API-based transaction reporting or digital stamping. VAT-liable documentation follows art. 26 VAT Act with mandatory invoice elements and 10-year retention. The legal payment instrument is the Swiss QR-bill (QR-Rechnung; fully applicable since 2022) and E-Bill (Peppol/CH-specific network) is contractually recognised; VAT returns are submitted electronically to the ESTV on a periodic basis (quarterly or semi-annually) through the e-fiscal portal with aggregate data, not invoice-by-invoice clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating applies under art. 53 VAT Act where durable/supplied movable goods are physically exported from Switzerland and the foreign recipient is established abroad; international transport services and ancillary services under art. 23 VAT Act are also 0% rated when used abroad. For the Free Trade Zone / Bonded Depot undertaking (customs-bonded storage), supplies of goods remain outside the VAT charge (suspended) until removal for export, which then qualifies for export zero rating provided the goods leave Swiss customs territory under the customs supervision of the Federal Customs Administration and the exporter retains conclusive evidence of the actual export movement.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Ausfuhrzollanmeldung) processed electronically via the Swiss customs clearance system 'e-dec GV' with confirmed export release
Transport evidence (CMR/air waybill or container track-and-trace record)
Bonded warehouse inventory register confirming physical removal
Depot operating licence of the Free Trade Zone (bewilligte Zolllager/zona franca licence)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under arts. 104–106 VAT Act, a groundless zero-rating claim triggers reassessment of statutory VAT with interest from the filing date and an administrative fine of up to 3 times the evaded tax; wilful fraud additionally carries criminal imprisonment of up to 3 years under art. 105 VAT Act plus publication of the penalty decision. Customs-related deficiencies (false or incomplete export declarations) are sanctioned under arts. 120–123 Customs Act with retrospective clawback of suspended duties, loss of the bonded warehouse licence, and disqualification from privileged VAT procedures; Swiss tax authorities may apply a 10-year limitation period for misuse cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) / Schweizerische Nationalbank, charged with monetary policy and national payment system oversight. Foreign exchange administration is not centralized; trade and capital flows fall under the general supervision of the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) and the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) for financial market policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions, with no exchange control restrictions under the Swiss Codification of Civil and Commercial Law or the Currency and Payment Instruments Act (CPIA). Dividend and profit remittance are not blocked, but a statutory 35% Swiss withholding tax applies to dividend distributions and similar payments; reduced treaty rates are available under Switzerland's DTA network. There are no licensing requirements for opening foreign currency accounts, entering into cross-border payments, or repatriating investment proceeds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Swiss law imposes no mandatory surrender of export proceeds, no conversion requirement, no repatriation timeline, and no requirement to hold export earnings in Swiss francs. Bonded warehouse operators may freely retain and reinvest export receipts in any currency. Only normal corporate income tax and VAT/reporting obligations apply, including the requirement to substantiate transactions with proper documentation and invoices.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-Medium. Foreign-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) and digital banks that lack a FINMA license generally cannot open operational corporate accounts with Swiss IBAN facilities for a Swiss-domiciled company. Switzerland permits a FINMA FinTech license for deposit-taking up to CHF 100 million without a full banking licence, and these entities can provide payment accounts for Swiss companies, but their cross-border clearing access is often limited. Fully offshore digital EMIs are generally treated as non-regulated intermediaries and cannot serve as the primary treasury account for a Swiss free zone bonded warehouse operator; they may be used only for auxiliary prepaid or virtual accounts, subject to the Swiss bank's AML aggregation rules.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical presence mandate is generally required for corporate account opening at Swiss tier-1 banks. In practice, at least one authorized signatory must appear in person for a KYC/AML interview for a newly incorporated Aktiengesellschaft. Remote video identification is occasionally allowed for privately held Swiss companies with straightforward ownership, but for a free trade zone bonded depot with cross-border trade flows, most banks require the beneficial owner to present in person at a Swiss branch or before a Swiss notary public with a notarized power of attorney. Digital onboarding with video interviews may be accepted by a limited number of fintech-licensed banks for operational accounts, but legacy tier-1 institutions will demand either an in-person meeting or an extended documentary evidence package.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner is a non-resident entity located in a non-EEA jurisdiction with unverifiable business background or opaque holding structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit endorsed shareholder register, chain-of-title diagram with certified corporate registry extracts from each intermediate jurisdiction, audited annual financials of the shareholder entity (if available), full beneficial ownership declaration confirmed by Swiss notarized signature, bank references from at least two regulated banks for the shareholders, and a structured economic substance evidence pack including office lease, payroll records, and business plan for the Swiss bonded depot.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bonded depot operations show high volumes of third-party payments or SWIFT wires from customers in high-risk jurisdictions or sanctions-embargoed countries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a 12-month customer and supplier diligence register with compliance classification, end-user certificates for all transactions, copies of valid customs bonding certificates, documentary evidence of goods stored (warehouse receipts, bills of lading), a sanctions screening log against the Swiss SECO and the EU/UN embargo lists, and an internal AML manual adhering to the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act including Article 13 CDB. The defense must include a clearance letter from the trade compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected cash-related deposit patterns from warehouse/manufacturing operations indicating potential intermingling of funds from non-booked sales or cargo sales outside customs procedures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce an independent auditor's report matching warehouse movement records to cash receipts, inventory management statements, customs declarations (e.g., NCTS Swiss Transit or ATA Carnets), signed lease for the warehouse, comprehensive insurance policy, and a detailed internal controls certification demonstrating transaction origination and matching of funds to specific commercial contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Currency risk management transactions believed to be speculative rather than commercially-backed hedging, especially in emerging-market currencies for bonded depot goods.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit treasury risk management policy with documented under-hedging and over-hedging limits; daily marked-to-market report; underlying trade contracts and invoices in the hedged currency; transfer pricing documentation if the trades are with related parties; board minutes authorising the FX hedging activity; and a validation report from the company's external risk consultant.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocols: SWIFT MT103 direct credit to the Swiss operating bank account of the Swiss AG with beneficiary matched to the corporate name and account opening identification. The payment reference field must include the statutory capital contribution reference (e.g., 'Einzahlung Aktienkapital / Paiement capital-actions') and corresponding board resolution reference if required. For a capital increase, the bank will verify the funds and issue an escrow release confirmation (Einzahlungsbestätigung). No exchange control approval is necessary; however, for amounts above CHF 15,000 the bank may request source-of-funds documentation (e.g., dividend distribution certificate, sale of assets, or financing agreement). For the execution of the capital escrow, banks require the funds to originate from the shareholder's own bank account bearing the shareholder's name; any third-party payment will create a high AML risk and likely delay release.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Preferred clearing rails: SWIFT MT103 (cover to underlying beneficiary bank) for direct supplier payments; SWIFT MT202 COV for settlement in other currencies; MT700/MT710 for commercial documentary credits in cross-border trade; SEPA Instant Credit (shorter clearing time) for EU/EEA counterparties in EUR; Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC) for same-day CHF domestic wires; Guarantee/Letter of Credit issuance via SWIFT MT760 or bank guarantee instrument in cases of pre-export financing or customs security. For bonded depot activities, disbursements for third-party trade settlement should reference the underlying invoice and customs declaration number to avoid bank querying anomalies. Local Swiss clearing rails for cash transactions and CHF remain SIC, while EUR payments may be cleared through EBA or Eurosystem TARGET2 depending on the bank's ECB access.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards with a standard ISDA/CSA master agreement, deliverable in CHF, EUR, USD, GBP and any major convertible currency
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currencies (e.g., CNY, INR, IDR, BRL) provided that the company can evidence underlying treasury exposure from bonded warehouse purchases or sales
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps) for asset-liability management, especially to hedge long-term capital injection proceeds or foreign-currency financing obligations
Vanilla FX options (European) to hedge trade-related exchange-rate risk in both delivered and non-delivered currencies
Cylinder / collared option strategies permitted only if executed through a FINMA-authorised Swiss bank or broker-dealer, with ISDA agreement and documented risk-management mandate

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting (AGM); approval and signing of annual financial statements; annual audit-opt-out resolution where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; corporate statutory records maintained at the registered office (no filing with the commercial register required for non-exempt companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the balance-sheet date (Art. 699 para. 2 CO); for a 31 December year-end: by 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court order on shareholder or creditor petition if the AGM is not convened; loss of audit-opt-out validity; no automatic administrative strike-off as no annual return is filed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax, federal direct tax and capital tax return (single consolidated filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration of the registered office canton (collects federal, cantonal and communal assessments)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: As set by the cantonal assessment notice; generally by 30 June after a calendar tax year (canton-specific; e.g., Geneva 31 May, Zurich 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at approximately 4.5-5% p.a.; late-filing procedural fine (typically up to CHF 10,000 per cantonal law); tax-evasion fine up to 3x evaded tax, with criminal proceedings for willful evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT self-declaration returns for Swiss federal VAT (8.1% standard rate in force)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly within 60 days after the end of the reporting quarter; semi-annual reporting is permitted for smaller taxable turnover volumes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest on deferred VAT; procedural fines up to CHF 30,000; tax-evasion fine up to 3x evaded VAT; forced collection through FTA enforcement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership (UBO) registration and change declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Central Beneficial Owners Register (operated under the Swiss AML regime by the federal authorities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: New AG: initial registration within 60 days of incorporation; any change in beneficial ownership within 60 days of gaining knowledge; no annual no-change filing is mandatory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML administrative penal procedure; fines and negative fit-and-proper assessment; in serious cases, criminal/AML sanctions and termination of banking relationships

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bonded warehouse / free trade zone licence: annual continuity declaration and customs account confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Office of Customs and Border Security (FOCBS/BAZG) - customs free-zone supervision unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Per licence conditions; generally an annual assurance aligned with the customs accounting period (calendar year) and due before 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension or revocation of the bonded-depot authorization; immediate customs-duty assessment on warehoused goods; customs penalty proceedings and default interest under the Swiss Customs Act

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary (full) audit is required if the AG exceeds two of three thresholds for two consecutive years: total assets ≥ CHF 20 million; gross turnover ≥ CHF 40 million; annual average ≥ 250 FTE, or if required for public/regulated activities (Art. 727 CO). Below those thresholds, a limited audit/review by a certified auditor applies unless the AG employs ≤10 FTE (annual average) and the shareholders pass an annual audit-opt-out resolution unanimously with no shareholder holding ≥10% of share capital demanding an auditor (Art. 727a/727b CO).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Statutory annual accounts per Swiss Code of Obligations (CO Arts. 957-963b), accrual-based; consolidated financial statements per Swiss GAAP FER or IFRS where consolidated; tax assessment follows the statutory balance sheet; business records retained for 10 years (Art. 958f CO).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law does not mandate a standalone annual UBO confirmation when no ownership change occurs; the company must maintain an accurate in-house UBO register and file any change (including registered-share transfers) with the Central Beneficial Owners Register within 60 days. As prudent corporate-governance practice and for banking AML reviews, an annual board-level attestation of the UBO schedule is recommended.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shareholders (Aktienbuch) with share-transfer annotations
Register of Directors and statutory officers
Minute books of Board and General Meeting
Commercial accounting records and business correspondence files

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200-3,500 per annum for registered office/domiciliation and corporate agent services in Zug/Zurich (typical market range)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000-12,000 for a Swiss limited audit/review performed by a licensed auditor; USD 0-1,500 incremental cost for audit-opt-out companies (≤10 FTE) using outsourced accounting

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal corporate income tax assessed on post-tax profit (effective rate approximately 7.83% of pre-tax profit); combined cantonal and communal municipal charge in Zug brings the aggregate ordinary statutory burden to approximately 11.9–12.0%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: TRAF (Swiss Tax Reform and AHV Financing, 2019): patent-box relief of up to 90% for qualifying IP income, optional additional 50% super-deduction for Swiss R&D, participation exemption for substantial shareholdings; no domestic free-trade-zone income-tax holiday exists — bonded warehouse profits are taxed at the ordinary rate, but customs duties and VAT remain suspended while goods are held under the customs warehousing procedure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined cantonal corporate income tax return for legal entities (Steuererklärung für juristische Personen) incorporating the Federal Direct Tax (Direkte Bundessteuer) schedule; electronic filing through the Canton Zug approved eTax/SwissTax software and the ESTV-compliant federal module.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after fiscal year-end (30 June for a 31 December balance sheet date); automatic extension to 31 December upon request, and further extension is regularly granted for professionally prepared audited filings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total turnover from bonded storage, stock management, handling, inspection, and other depot services invoiced during the reporting period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Swiss-source revenue attributable to the Swiss licensed depot; sales and storage invoiced through the foreign principal remain outside the Swiss return unless the depot creates a Swiss permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section A, Box 2 — Bonded goods on hand
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Position for customs-suspended inventories held in the free trade zone / customs warehouse; these goods are not treated as taxable assets of the Aktiengesellschaft.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners of the bonded goods are not required to report the inventory in the Swiss tax return; the AG discloses only business assets related to services, not the stored goods.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section B, Box 3 — Net taxable profit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory profit per Swiss Code of Obligations accounts (Art. 957 et seq. CO), adjusted for non-deductible items, hidden profit distributions, and transfer pricing corrections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Prepare accounts on an arm's-length basis; interest-free balances owed to the foreign parent must be re-characterised as deemed interest or constructive dividends if not contractually documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section B, Box 4 — Director fees and related-party charges
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fees paid to board members, management, and group entities; only customary, documented, and adequately supported amounts are deductible.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to non-resident directors and foreign related parties require transfer pricing documentation and beneficial-owner evidence if challenged.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section C, Box 5 — Withholding tax credits and refunds
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Swiss federal withholding tax previously borne on dividends and taxable interest received by the AG is creditable against the corporate income tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The AG applies for reimbursement of the Swiss withholding tax credit; the non-resident parent's treaty refund on its own dividend allocation is handled separately with the Federal Tax Administration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section D, Box 6 — TRAF special reliefs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Patent box, R&D super-deduction, and notional interest deduction (where the canton has enacted the option) claimed in the relevant schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a pure bonded warehouse operator, R&D relief will rarely apply unless the company develops proprietary warehouse-management software; a conservative claim supported by a tax ruling is recommended.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Bring forward of unused tax losses from earlier years: losses are deductible against future profits for seven assessment periods; no carry-back exists.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss attributes remain available to the same legal entity only; a transfer of the AG or of the bonded depot licence does not automatically preserve losses against new unrelated business.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Procedural fine for untimely filing up to CHF 10,000 under Art. 174 DBG and cantonal equivalents; default assessment with 3.5% annual federal interest and cantonal late-payment surcharges; deliberate late submission after reminders is treated as evasion and triggers a penalty of 1 to 3 times the tax evaded.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Verrechnungssteuer (Swiss withholding tax) on AG dividends, levied at source on distribution; refundable to Swiss-resident shareholders and reduced or refunded under a double taxation agreement to non-residents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder files a refund or relief application with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) using the official series of forms (Form 823 family) and supplies a current Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the shareholder's jurisdiction together with proof of beneficial ownership; the paying AG may alternatively obtain an advance exemption-from-withholding clearance under the VStV procedure. Claims are time-barred after three years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: Swiss WHT of 35% applies only to taxable bonds and Swiss bank interest; ordinary intra-group loans pay interest free of Swiss withholding tax. Royalties: Switzerland imposes no withholding tax on outbound royalty payments. Under most Swiss DTAs, cross-border interest is reduced or eliminated and royalties are taxable only in the residence state at 0%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory Swiss Local File or Master File thresholds exist; the ESTV and cantonal tax administrations apply OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines and request documentation when related-party transactions exceed commercial materiality (in practice after related-party turnover above approximately CHF 500,000–1,000,000); a mandatory Country-by-Country Report notification and filing arises for Swiss MNE groups with consolidated group revenue of at least CHF 900 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland applies a centre-of-administration residency test and an economic-substance review for treaty entitlements and withholding-tax refunds; a letterbox vehicle lacks substance. A free-trade-zone bonded depot operated as an AG with permanent local management, warehouse staff, customs-bonded full records, office premises, and locally documented pricing decisions satisfies the administrative practice; the Swiss treaty network embeds OECD PPT/LOB clauses, so the depot's actual warehousing function is decisive.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion — under-declared income / false returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a materially false or incomplete Swiss tax return, backdating or destroying depot records, invoicing warehouse commissions partially and holding undeclared cash generated in the bonded depot, or maintaining an apparent foreign administration that masks actual Swiss management of the CH_AG.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imposition of the evaded tax plus interest and a fine from one to three times the evaded amount under Art. 175 DBG; repeated, wilful, and concealed evasion is prosecuted as tax fraud under Art. 186 DBG with custodial penalties up to three years and forfeiture of unjust gains.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members and the managing director who participated in or tolerated the evasion are personally liable under Art. 754 CO for resulting company losses; individuals face criminal fines, imprisonment, and the use of Swiss mutual legal assistance — passport confiscation and travel restrictions may follow upon formal extradition proceedings outside Switzerland.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring the depot's cash flows as interest-free shareholder loans, paying non-arm's-length management fees to the foreign parent, assuming the parent's costs through the bonded warehouse company, or paying excessive rent or storage prices to a related party without documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authority recasts the advantage as a constructive dividend: additional corporate income tax, 35% withholding tax exposure at source, default interest, and potential evasion fines; the AG loses deductibility of the underlying payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The shareholder is personally taxable on the deemed dividend; directors who approved the transaction cannot rely on the corporate veil and may be jointly liable for the 35% withheld tax and for civil restitution of diverted assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell / letterbox company and treaty abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Zug AG with no full-time employees, no local board activity, and no real depot management, while routing foreign shareholder dividend claims through the AG to secure refunds and Swiss DTA benefits; or using the free-trade-zone bonded licence solely as a pass-through booking centre.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, refund disallowed, and 35% Swiss withholding tax imposed; civil interest and fines for misuse; in international structures the authorities may reallocate profits entirely outside the Swiss entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly maintained the conduit structure face accessory liability for Swiss withholding taxes not withheld and enhanced fines; insolvency proceedings could subsequently expose the founders through liability rules for undercapitalised corporations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / customs and VAT abuse in the bonded depot
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting cargo without customer due diligence and beneficial-owner verification, settling storage fees in cash, subletting the warehouse licence to unverified third parties, entering false exit declarations, diverting free-zone goods into Swiss free circulation without VAT settlement, or laundering criminal proceeds through the depot's cash flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs authorities assess unpaid duties and 8.1% VAT plus customs-evasion fines of up to the duty or tax evaded in aggravated cases; violations of the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act carry administrative fines of up to CHF 500,000, and criminal money laundering under Art. 305bis StGB carries imprisonment up to three years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who fail to install an effective AML framework at the depot are criminally exposed; confiscation of corporate and personal assets, director disqualification measures, and, upon criminal conviction, enforceable imprisonment or extradition affecting the right to travel internationally.
